condition: Acute appendicitis in the third trimester
permutationLabel: 32 weeks, right upper quadrant/flank pain, MRI-confirmed
summary: 31-year-old G3P2 at 32 weeks with 24 h of right upper quadrant/flank pain (displaced appendix), T 37.9, HR 108, WBC 16.2, CRP 88; US non-diagnostic, MRI: inflamed appendix. Laparoscopic appendicectomy with obstetric input and fetal monitoring; no NSAIDs.

inputs.hpi: G3P2 at 32 weeks. 24 hours of right-sided abdominal pain, now constant under the right ribs and in the right flank, nausea and anorexia. No vaginal bleeding, no contractions, fetal movements normal. Urine: trace leucocytes only.

exam.abdomen: Gravid uterus, fundus 32 cm, soft and non-tender, no contractions. Tender right flank and right upper quadrant lateral to the uterus with guarding. Fetal heart 145/min on Doppler.

labs.name: Urine dipstick
labs.resultText: Leucocytes trace, nitrite negative, protein negative

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallbladder normal, no stones. Right kidney mild physiological hydronephrosis. Appendix not visualised.

imaging.name: MRI abdomen (non-contrast)
imaging.result: Dilated 11 mm appendix displaced superiorly to the right flank with wall thickening and periappendiceal inflammatory change; no abscess.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute appendicitis at 32 weeks' gestation (MRI-confirmed)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute uncomplicated appendicitis at 32 weeks, MRI-confirmed. Laparoscopic appendicectomy with left lateral tilt; obstetric team, CTG before and after surgery; avoid NSAIDs.

mustInclude.note: Viable fetus at 32 weeks: obstetric team and fetal heart/contraction monitoring before and after surgery.

mustExclude.note: NSAIDs are avoided from 20 weeks (fetal renal dysfunction, oligohydramnios, ductal constriction in the third trimester).
She is 32 weeks pregnant: a template stating "β-HCG confirmed negative" is false and dangerous.

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Pregnancy: ultrasound first, MRI if inconclusive; laparoscopic appendicectomy in pregnancy; children: ultrasound first, clinical scores (PAS), antibiotics and appendicectomy for complicated appendicitis
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S, Podda M, De Simone B, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:27.

guideline.name: SAGES guidelines for the use of laparoscopy during pregnancy
guideline.section: Laparoscopic appendicectomy may be performed in any trimester; left lateral positioning to limit aortocaval compression; pre- and post-operative fetal heart monitoring; obstetric consultation
guideline.citation: Pearl JP, Price RR, Tonkin AE, Richardson WS, Stefanidis D. SAGES guidelines for the use of laparoscopy during pregnancy. Surg Endosc. 2017;31:3767–3782.

guideline.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 775 — nonobstetric surgery during pregnancy
guideline.section: Obstetric consultation before non-obstetric surgery; with a viable fetus, at minimum electronic fetal heart rate and contraction monitoring before and after the procedure
guideline.citation: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. Nonobstetric surgery during pregnancy: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 775. Obstet Gynecol. 2019;133:e285–e286.

guideline.name: FDA drug safety communication — NSAIDs at 20 weeks or later in pregnancy
guideline.section: Avoid NSAIDs from 20 weeks of pregnancy (fetal renal dysfunction, oligohydramnios; ductal constriction later in pregnancy)
guideline.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. FDA recommends avoiding use of NSAIDs in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later because they can result in low amniotic fluid. Drug Safety Communication, 15 October 2020.

rationale: In the third trimester the appendix is displaced upwards, so pain is right-sided or subcostal. Laparoscopic appendicectomy is appropriate in any trimester, with obstetric involvement and fetal monitoring for a viable fetus, left lateral positioning and no NSAIDs.
